 Profit by Pakistan Today • 16 Nov 2026, 10:00 AM PKT • 1 min read 
 ENG اردو A- A+ Add as preferred source on Google X f President Asif Ali Zardari has rejected the Federal Board of Revenue’s challenge to a recommendation for automated income tax refunds, upholding the proposal for a Faceless Refund Regime. The case concerned a Rs42.86 million refund claim for tax year 2025, which remained under verification.
 The recommendation calls on the FBR to create a process under Section 170A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, to approve and electronically transfer verified tax-credit refunds to taxpayers’ notified bank accounts without requiring formal applications. Profit by Pakistan Today reported that the FBR had argued the taxpayer could appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals), but the President maintained the recommendation, citing the need to ease delays and administrative steps.
 At a glance
 The President dismissed the FBR’s representation over the refund case.
 The proposal would electronically transfer verified refunds without formal applications.
 The claim involved Rs42.86 million for tax year 2025.
 Why it matters
 The proposed process concerns the recovery of income tax refunds, an issue relevant to taxpayers and businesses managing cash flows.
